decisions.reason: The approved 3000 RPM adjustable motor selection and removal of the prior 1500 RPM constraint are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The source approves motor speed and physical accommodation but establishes no new wiring configuration or electrical specification; the basic wiring-plan requirement remains unchanged.
The 3000 RPM maximum, adjustable range, and intended speed modes are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The requirement that high-speed mixing remain smooth rather than overly aggressive is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The accepted prolonged-use expectation and prohibition on constant maximum-speed operation are already represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE.
High-speed splash control and the accepted mitigation options are already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
Approval of larger, faster motors does not explicitly alter the existing stability or vibration-control behavior.
Selecting the proposed 3000 RPM motors does not change the existing strategy of using off-the-shelf electronics for the first prototype.
The client only permits bowl-depth adjustment if needed for splash control and does not require an actual change to the approved bowl size or geometry.
The motor and CAD accommodation decision does not change the dispensing mechanism, sequence, flow behavior, or control requirements.
The approved motor direction does not alter the existing leak-free seal requirements.
The source decision does not alter the requirement to isolate electrical components from leaking liquid.
